Findings: There is a rounded or semilunar subcortical right, posterior parieto-occipital, smoothly marginated hypodense mass measuring 2.4 x 1.7 cm that is isodense with CSF, with its medial border formed by overlying cortical parenchyma and a possible mural nodule. There is peripheral decreased white matter attenuation throughout the posterior right parietal white matter, as well as anterolaterally and medially to the paracentral region, with mass effect resulting in effacement of the overlying sulci, consistent with vasogenic edema. Within the posterior left parietal lobe at the vertex, a new focus of parenchymal edema is observed, containing a 4.5 x 9.0 mm focus of hemorrhage. There is no cingulate, uncal, or hippocampal herniation. Moderate dilatation of the lateral and third ventricles is present; the third ventricle is enlarged in a configuration consistent with thalamic atrophy. The subarachnoid spaces are diffusely widened, but maintain normal CSF density. Periventricular decreased attenuation, centered on the angles of the lateral ventricles and merging with decreased white matter attenuation throughout the centrum semiovale bilaterally, is consistent with microangiopathy. The third and fourth ventricles remain midline. Mild, symmetric widening of the cerebellar folia indicates cerebellar atrophy. Atherosclerotic cavernous carotid and distal vertebral arterial wall calcifications are noted. The paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are normally aerated, and the bony calvarium is intact.
Impression: Cystic right posterior parietal mass with disproportionate vasogenic edema that is increasing. There is a new, small focus of vasogenic edema associated with a subcentimeter overlying cortical hyperdense mass in the left posteromedial parietal lobe. Differential diagnosis includes metastatic disease, multicentric glioma, and primary intracranial lymphoma, with inflammatory (e.g., viral) etiologies considered less likely. Correlation with MRI of the brain with and without gadolinium is recommended. Additionally, there is underlying cerebral cortical, thalamic, and cerebellar atrophy, with aging demyelination and chronic ischemic microvascular disease. The bony calvarium is intact.
